Name: Monolith
When to Use: Early product, single team, fast iteration, unclear domain boundaries
When NOT to Use: Many independent teams competing for one repo/release, needs polyglot scaling
Strengths: Simple deploy, easy refactor across modules, strong consistency by default, single observability target
Weaknesses: Scaling discipline (modules), large blast radius, slow CI as it grows
Notes: Default for new products. Modularise internally with strict module boundaries (ArchUnit, internal packages).

Name: Modular Monolith
When to Use: Want monolith ops simplicity but need clear domain boundaries to prepare for future split
When NOT to Use: If team is already split with conflicting release cadences
Strengths: Strong domain boundaries inside one process; can split later
Weaknesses: Discipline required to avoid 'big ball of mud'
Notes: Use module-internal package visibility + ArchUnit/Spectral/Dependency Cruiser to enforce boundaries.

Name: Microservices
When to Use: Multiple independent teams with separate release cadences; need polyglot or independent scaling
When NOT to Use: Tiny teams; unclear domain boundaries; immature observability/CI
Weaknesses: Operational complexity (deploy/observe/secure many services), distributed-system bugs, costlier
Notes: Don't go below ~1 service per 8-engineer team. Invest in platform (CI/CD, mesh, observability) FIRST.

Name: Serverless (FaaS)
When to Use: Spiky / unpredictable traffic, glue code, scheduled tasks, event-driven side effects
When NOT to Use: Steady high RPS where cold starts hurt; long-running CPU work
Strengths: Scales to zero, no servers, fine-grained cost
Weaknesses: Cold starts, vendor lock-in, debugging/local-dev story
Keywords: lambda cloud functions step functions eventbridge
Notes: Pair Lambda + EventBridge + Step Functions for event-driven without K8s.

Name: Event-Driven Architecture
When to Use: Loose coupling between services; complex workflows; need to broadcast state changes
When NOT to Use: Synchronous request/response with strict latency SLOs
Strengths: Loose coupling, scalability, audit trail, fan-out
Weaknesses: Eventual consistency, harder to reason about, requires schema discipline
Notes: Combine with schema registry (Confluent / Buf / EventBridge Schema Registry); design events as past-tense facts.

Name: Hexagonal / Ports & Adapters
When to Use: Want testable domain isolated from frameworks/IO
When NOT to Use: Trivial CRUD where indirection adds no value
Strengths: Testable domain, easy to swap adapters
Weaknesses: Boilerplate; over-engineered if domain is thin
Notes: Pair with DDD bounded contexts; persist via 'repository' adapter, not active record.

Name: Clean Architecture / Onion
When to Use: Same as hexagonal, with explicit layered concentric model
Notes: Slight over-prescription vs hexagonal; pick one and be consistent.

Name: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) / Bounded Contexts
When to Use: Complex business domain with multiple subdomains
Strengths: Aligns code with business; clear ownership; basis for service split
Weaknesses: Steep learning curve; requires domain experts on the team
Keywords: ddd domain driven bounded context aggregate
Notes: Strategic DDD (context maps) > tactical patterns. Use ContextMaps to plan microservice splits.

Name: CQRS + Event Sourcing
When to Use: Audit-heavy domains, complex temporal queries, very read/write asymmetric
When NOT to Use: Simple CRUD with no audit need
Strengths: Full history, replay, separate read/write scaling
Weaknesses: Eventual consistency, schema evolution, ops complexity
Notes: Combine with snapshots & projections; choose only when audit/temporal queries are core.

Name: Service Mesh + Microservices
When to Use: Many services on K8s needing mTLS, retries, traffic shifting, observability without code changes
Strengths: Cross-cutting concerns out of code; consistent policy
Keywords: istio linkerd cilium ambient mesh mtls
Notes: Linkerd for simplicity; Istio Ambient or Cilium Mesh to reduce sidecar overhead via eBPF.

Name: BFF (Backend for Frontend)
When to Use: Multiple clients (web/mobile/IoT) with divergent shape needs
Strengths: Tailored APIs per client; insulates clients from backend churn
Weaknesses: Duplicated aggregation across BFFs; potential N+1
Keywords: bff backend for frontend graphql aggregator
Notes: GraphQL is a popular BFF technology; tRPC works for TS-only stacks.

Name: Lambda / Kappa Architecture
When to Use: Data lake with both batch + real-time consumers
Strengths: Lambda: separate batch + speed layer; Kappa: stream-only
Weaknesses: Lambda has duplicate code paths; Kappa needs strong stream infra
Notes: Modern stacks (Iceberg/Delta + Flink/Spark) make Kappa increasingly attractive.

Name: Actor Model
When to Use: Stateful, conversational, per-entity logic at scale (gaming, IoT, simulation)
Weaknesses: Programming model shift; debugging distributed actors is hard
Keywords: actor model akka pekko orleans elixir erlang
Notes: Akka/Pekko (JVM), Orleans (.NET), Elixir/OTP (BEAM) — pick based on language.

Name: Cell-Based Architecture
When to Use: Hyperscale SaaS needing strong blast-radius isolation
Strengths: Each 'cell' is fully isolated stack; capped failure domain
Keywords: cell based architecture aws shuffle sharding
Notes: See AWS Builders' Library 'Workload isolation using shuffle-sharding' & cell-based architecture papers.
